chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleym, the mawla of Tirbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had intercourse with his slave girl, and that he used to send her for his needs, and that she became pregnant, and that he accused her and news of her mischief reached him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When she gives birth, he should keep the child and not sell him, and make for him a share from his house [and his wealth]'

He said, 'It was said to him: A man had intercourse with his slave girl, and that he had not sent her for his needs, and that he accused her, and she became pregnant.' So he said: 'When she gives birth, he should keep the child and not sell him, and make for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this is not similar to that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child born to a slave girl from her master in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the legal status of the 'Umm al-Walad' (mother of the child) and her offspring, emphasizing that the child’s freedom and inheritance rights are secured regardless of whether the mother was actively employed or merely accused of misconduct. The distinction drawn by Imam Al-Sadiq highlights the nuanced application of evidence in determining the father's obligation to retain the child and allocate a share of his estate, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on protecting the lineage and status of concubine-born children.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleym, a slave of Tirbal, from Hareyz,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who went to his slave girl of his, and he had sent her somewhere regarding a need of his, and she became pregnant, and he accused her and news of her mischief reached him. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When she gives birth, she should keep the child and not sell him, and make for him a share from his house and his wealth’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man went to a slave girl of his, and he had not sent her regarding a need of his, and he accused her, and she was pregnant’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When she gives birth, he should keep the child and not sell him, and make for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this is not similar to that’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad from Salim Mawla Tirbal from Hariz who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who goes to bed with his slave-girl and sends her to do certain works for him. She becomes pregnant; he [accuses] her and receives news of her misbehaving. He (the Imam) said, ‘When she gives birth he must keep the child and must not sell him but assign for him a share from his house [and assets].’

It was then asked about a man who goes to bed with his slave-girl, does not send her to work for him but he accuses her of misbehaving and she becomes pregnant. He (the Imam) said, ‘When she gives birth he must keep the child and must not sell but assign a share for the child from his house and assets. This is not like that.’”
